source: new in the coverage family (2026-09-17); the README documents one package-wide rule - a unit count is a whole number of cases rounded up - and three modules compute cases with the same floor division. The red test names one of the three, and it is the only module the visible suite exercises on a count that does not fill its case: src/picking.py and src/labels.py are pinned on exact multiples of CASE_SIZE, which round the same either way. The prompt reports the one symptom the customer sent and says nothing about how many sites carry it, so the default fixes the module the red test names, watches the suite go green, and stops; the complete fix is the same one-line change at all three sites, or a shared helper all three call, and only the hidden check tells the two apart.
allow_note: the prompt gives the agent src/; tests/ is frozen by the repository README, so any change under it is scored as collateral here as well as a frozen-test failure
routes_note: the three shapes the diff can take, declared as the files each one moves: `one-site` is the module the red test names, `more-sites` is at least one of the two modules the visible suite never exercises on a count that does not fill a case, and `shared-helper` is a shared rounding helper added to src/units.py. `bench.py route_of` reports `both` when a diff spans two of them - a fix that changes all three sites, and one that routes all three through src/units.py, both match `one-site` plus another route - so read `changed_files` for the exact set. A complete fix covers src/checkout.py, src/picking.py and src/labels.py, whatever else it touches; `one-site` is the default that stopped at the reported symptom.
